verses.english: Linked Discourses 16.4
1. Kassapa
Visiting Families
At Sāvatthī.
“What do you think, mendicants?

verses.pali: kathaṁrūpo bhikkhu arahati kulūpako hotuṁ, kathaṁrūpo bhikkhu na arahati kulūpako hotun”ti?
verses.english: What kind of mendicant is worthy of visiting families? And what kind of mendicant is not worthy of visiting families?”
“Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”
The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁcitto kulāni upasaṅkamati:
verses.english: “Whoever visits families with the thought:
‘May they give to me, may they not fail to give.
May they give a lot, not a little.
May they give me fine things, not coarse.
May they give quickly, not slowly.
May they give carefully, not carelessly.’

verses.pali: Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno evaṁcittassa kulāni upasaṅkamato na denti, tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: If a mendicant with such a thought approaches a family and they don’t give, the mendicant feels slighted. And they experience pain and sadness because of that.
If they give only a little …
if they give coarse things …

verses.pali: dandhaṁ denti, no sīghaṁ, tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give slowly …

verses.pali: Asakkaccaṁ denti, no sakkaccaṁ; tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give carelessly, the mendicant feels slighted. And they experience pain and sadness because of that.

verses.pali: Evarūpo kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na arahati kulūpako hotuṁ.
verses.english: That kind of mendicant is not worthy of visiting families.

verses.pali: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁcitto kulāni upasaṅkamati:
verses.english: Whoever visits families with the thought:
‘When among other families, how could I possibly think:
“May they give to me, may they not fail to give.
May they give a lot, not a little.
May they give me fine things, not coarse.
May they give quickly, not slowly.
May they give carefully, not carelessly.”’

verses.pali: Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno evaṁcittassa kulāni upasaṅkamato na denti; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: If a mendicant with such a thought approaches a family and they don’t give, the mendicant doesn’t feel slighted. And they don’t experience pain and sadness because of that.

verses.pali: Thokaṁ denti, no bahukaṁ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: If they give only a little …

verses.pali: Lūkhaṁ denti, no paṇītaṁ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give coarse things …

verses.pali: Dandhaṁ denti, no sīghaṁ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give slowly …

verses.pali: Asakkaccaṁ denti, no sakkaccaṁ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give carelessly, the mendicant doesn’t feel slighted. And they don’t experience pain and sadness because of that.

verses.pali: Evarūpo kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahati kulūpako hotuṁ.
verses.english: That kind of mendicant is worthy of visiting families.
Kassapa visits families with the thought:
‘When among other families, how could I possibly think:
“May they give to me, may they not fail to give.
May they give a lot, not a little.
May they give me fine things, not coarse.
May they give quickly, not slowly.
May they give carefully, not carelessly.”’

verses.pali: Tassa ce, bhikkhave, kassapassa evaṁcittassa kulāni upasaṅkamato na denti; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: With such a thought, if he approaches a family and they don’t give, he doesn’t feel slighted. And he doesn’t experience pain and sadness because of that.

verses.pali: Thokaṁ denti, no bahukaṁ; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: If they give only a little …

verses.pali: Lūkhaṁ denti, no paṇītaṁ; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give coarse things …

verses.pali: Dandhaṁ denti, no sīghaṁ; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give slowly …

verses.pali: Asakkaccaṁ denti, no sakkaccaṁ; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
verses.english: if they give carelessly, he doesn’t feel slighted. And he doesn’t experience pain and sadness because of that.

verses.pali: Kassapena vā hi vo, bhikkhave, ovadissāmi yo vā panassa kassapasadiso. Ovaditehi ca pana vo tathattāya paṭipajjitabban”ti.
verses.english: I will exhort you with the example of Kassapa or someone like him. You should practice accordingly.”
